newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul arrests wanted student leader, 23 activists.
newsitem.headline: Seoul arrests wanted student leader, 23 activists.

text.p: South Korean police on Monday arrested a student leader wanted on suspicion organising a violent student protest in August, a police official said.

Park Byoung-un, 23, a leader of the outlawed Hanchongryon (a student activist organisation), was arrested with 23 other students while they were gathering for a meeting at a Seoul university campus, he said.
"The 24 people are now being questioned here," the official at the Seoul Police Agency said by telephone. He declined to give further details.

More than 3,000 students were arrested in August after riot police stormed the Yonsei University campus to end seven days of occupation. The students were demanding reunification with North Korea and the withdrawal of U.S. troops from the South.

Of those arrested, 444 have been put on trial on charges ranging from violation of the National Security Law to acts of violence and interference with police duties. The trials are expected to be concluded by the end of this month.
